content.title: About
content.content: Cheese pizza is a popular fast‑food and restaurant dish consisting of a crust topped with tomato sauce and a generous layer of melted cheese. Mozzarella is most common, but cheddar, parmesan, or a blend of cheeses are often used.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheese pizza was made in Naples in the 19th century.
The most popular crust type for cheese pizza is thin crust, though deep‑dish is common in the United States.
More than 30 varieties of cheese can be used, each giving a distinct flavor and texture.
In Japan, cheese pizza is frequently garnished with seaweed and mayonnaise.
In 2012, over 3 billion servings of cheese pizza were sold in the United States.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese provides a good amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: The cheese layer supplies complete animal protein that supports tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory compounds
items.content: Certain cheeses (e.g., mozzarella) contain conjugated linoleic acid, which may help reduce inflammation.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Hard cheeses such as parmesan can contain live cultures that support gut microbiota.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty, and excessive intake can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Large portions of cheese pizza can increase saturated fat consumption, which may affect heart health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after eating regular cheese pizza.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to casein, a protein found in cheese.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese pizza is typically eaten hot, sliced into wedges. Additional toppings such as ham, vegetables, or herbs can be added. For a lighter option, choose whole‑grain crust and reduce the amount of cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2–3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore a crisp crust. Pizza can be frozen for up to 2 months if wrapped tightly in plastic film.
